title: Intraoperative Measurement of Insertion Forces During Conventional Cochlear Implantation and First Characterization of Interindividual In Vivo Variability
summary: Ziel der Studie ist die Messung der auftretenden Kräfte beim Einführen des Elektrodenträgers eines Cochlea-Implantats (CI) in die Hörschnecke bei ansonsten unveränderter chirurgischer Technik (was insbesondere das manuelle Halten und Führen des Elektrodenträgers betrifft = „konventionelles Vorgehen“) und daraus ableitend die erstmalige Beschreibung der interindividuellen Variabilität der humanen in vivo Insertionskräfte in einem größeren Patientenkollektiv. Dafür soll ein an der MHH entwickeltes, kraftsensorisches Insertionstools intraoperativ genutzt werden. Ziel der in vivo Insertionskraftmessung im Rahmen dieser Studie ist die Aufzeichnung der Insertionskräfte bei einer größeren Anzahl von Patientinnen und Patienten und in einer homogeneren und damit repräsentativeren Patientengruppe für die Bestimmung der mittleren Insertionskräfte beim Menschen. Aus den erfassten Daten soll die „ground truth“ für die Insertionskräfte bei manueller, konventioneller Insertion durch erfahrene Chirurginnen und Chirurgen beschrieben werden, die für zahlreiche zukünftige wissenschaftliche und klinische Fragestellungen von fundamentaler Bedeutung ist.

interventions.name: Adult patients (m/f/d), aged ≥18 years, who are scheduled to receive a cochlear implant based on a medical indication. For cochlear implantation, either an electrode array from the Flex series manufactured by MED-EL or a cochlear implant manufactured by Cochlear with a Slim Straight electrode array

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Adult patients (m/f/d), aged ≥ 18 years, who are scheduled to receive a cochlear implant (i.e., who meet the applicable indication criteria)
- Patient information and consent for conventional cochlear implant surgery have been obtained
- Either a MED-EL cochlear implant with a Flex series electrode array or a cochlear implant manufactured by Cochlear with a Slim Straight electrode array will be implanted
- Surgical clearance has been granted by the anesthesiology team for general anesthesia via intubation, analgosedation, or local anesthesia
Exclusion criteria:
- All patients who do not meet the inclusion criteria
- Anatomical abnormalities (e.g., of the inner ear or mastoid) or signs of intracochlear ossification or severe otosclerosis which, in the surgeon’s assessment, contraindicate the use of the force-sensing insertion tool
- Patients in whom, following posterior tympanotomy, the facial nerve and/or chorda tympani are no longer covered by bone (i.e., the nerve is no longer completely covered by a layer of bone that would otherwise effectively protect it from damage caused by the insertion tool)
- Reimplantation
- Patients who are already participating in another study that could influence the forces acting during CI electrode insertion
- Children
- Pregnant or breastfeeding women
- Patients receiving palliative care
- Individuals unable to provide informed consent due to an acute illness
- Individuals unable to provide informed consent due to a chronic illness
- Persons placed under institutional care by a public authority
- Nursing home residents
- Patients who do not provide written informed consent for the use of the force-sensing insertion tool
